topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the primary conventional modalities of cancer treatment—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—and the challenges of toxicity and resistance associated with them.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and defects in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss therapeutic strategies that take advantage of specific tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, resistance, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the development of small-molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the mechanisms of resistance and drug addiction that arise during treatment.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They cover therapeutic approaches that utilize engineered antibodies to directly target tumor cell surface antigens or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the evidence for immune surveillance and the mechanisms of T-cell-harnessing therapies such as immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic progress, future directions, and ethical considerations
topics.groupedBecause: They assess the overall challenges, historical outcomes, emerging paradigms, and ethical dilemmas facing modern cancer management.
